News: Tesla Optimus robot enters factory production line

HOOK: Tesla's robot just started working on the factory floor. For real this time.

BODY: Optimus isn't a demo anymore. It's picking up parts, sorting inventory, and doing repetitive tasks alongside human workers at Tesla's Fremont factory. Musk says 1,000 Optimus units will be deployed by 2026, with a target price of $20K each. That's cheaper than a year's salary for any factory worker on Earth. The humanoid robot era isn't coming. It's here.

HOOK: Apple just put a full AI brain inside your iPhone. No internet needed.

HOOK: A 16-year-old just built a million-dollar AI company. From his bedroom.

News: EU passes comprehensive AI regulation law

HOOK: The EU just made it illegal to use AI in ways that 90% of companies already do.

BODY: The EU AI Act is here. High-risk AI systems now need mandatory audits before deployment. Social scoring is banned. Real-time facial recognition in public spaces is restricted. Companies have 2 years to comply or face fines up to 7% of global revenue. That's $14 billion for a company like Google. The question isn't whether this changes AI. It's whether it pushes innovation out of Europe entirely.

News: Free AI coding assistant outperforms GitHub Copilot in benchmarks

HOOK: A free AI coding tool just destroyed GitHub Copilot in every benchmark. And nobody's talking about it.

BODY: It's called Cody by Sourcegraph. Open source, free, and it just scored 15% higher than Copilot on HumanEval. The secret? It indexes your entire codebase, understands your architecture, and generates code that actually fits your project. Not generic suggestions. Context-aware completions. It works in VS Code, JetBrains, and Neovim. The $19/month you're paying for Copilot? You might not need to.
